assumptions.text: the temp family is keyed by PANE id and carries the placement alone — { [paneId]: { size } } — so the ghost's question is asked at the node that names the pane
assumptions.alternative: keying it by GESTURE id (the gate-era temp.drag.<gestureId>.placement), which makes the address name a gesture the ghost cannot ask about and leaves the reading with no reader (D-132, D-133)

assumptions.text: ending the reading is a DELETE at the family's own tier, so the address answers absent after the gesture
assumptions.alternative: clearing it by writing an empty family, which leaves a temp node standing and makes 'gone' weaker than row 5's word (D-101, row 5)

assumptions.text: the ghost is a DECLARED TRANSIENT declaration on the pane element the wiring already holds — spelled data-ghost="temp", present while the reading names the pane at temp and removed otherwise — observed through provident.get_rendered_html
assumptions.alternative: a graph props write, which re-renders the pane mid-gesture — the re-render hazard D-117's declared transient style write exists to avoid (D-117)

assumptions.text: two routes (commitDrag, clearDrag) rather than one carrying a null arm
assumptions.alternative: one route with a null argument for the erase, which the store's boundary refuses (measured) and which is the spelling D-140 spent a row removing (D-140)
